thread:
Alex W: Quick summary of the morning perf run for the continuous-batcher + scheduler changes across APAC (h100) and EU (a100).
Maria P: awesome — top-level numbers?
Alex W: p50/p95 token-latency and throughput for the new window pacing + max_batch_tokens logic
Alex W: APAC h100 (cont-batcher, batch_window_ms=30, max_batch_tokens=8192): p50=12ms/token, p95=42ms/token, throughput=6.2k tokens/s per GPU
Alex W: EU a100 (cont-batcher, batch_window_ms=30, max_batch_tokens=8192): p50=18ms/token, p95=68ms/token, throughput=4.0k tokens/s per GPU
Samir K: interesting delta. kernel picks?
Alex W: h100 picked flash_attn2 fused kernels, a100 fell back to tiled_attention for large sequence lengths (seq~2048) — we saw kernel fallback at ~6% of requests in EU
Deepak R: did you run quantized variants too?
Alex W: yes — int8 dynamic quant on both. int8 reduced throughput by ~3% on h100 (kernel overhead) but improved cost. On a100 int8 helped more: +10% throughput vs fp16 because tiled kernels benefited from smaller memory footprint.
Maria P: fairness across tenants? any starving cohorts after pacing change?
Alex W: ran a 12h mixed-tenant replay. We added priority decay (10% per minute) and soft-tilt fairness. Result: tail latency for low-priority cohort increased 8% but throughput isolation held; no SLA breaches in canary group.
Samir K: what about batching behavior distribution? any long tails in batch sizes?
Alex W: batch size distribution shifted: mean tokens/batch +22%, median +18%, long tail reduced due to pacing. We still see microbursts where max_batch_tokens hit cap; those correlate with large-context requests.
Deepak R: did bench-bot capture kernel timings and KV cache hit rates?
bench-bot: Attached snapshot: kv_cache_hit_rate=0.71, avg_kernel_time_flash=9.5ms, avg_kernel_time_tiled=16.2ms, cont_batch_wait=18ms
Alex W: action items: (1) try lowering batch_window_ms to 20ms in EU canary to reduce p95, (2) add a kernel hint for a100 to prefer fp16 tiled path when seq<1024, (3) run a 24h mixed quantization run to validate quality regressions (note: we saw 0.6% BLEU-like regression on internal eval set for int8)
Maria P: +1. For (3) add evals against the production prompt set and regression alert if >0.5%
Samir K: I can take (2). will push a config and schedule a sweep for seq cutover hints.
Deepak R: I'll own (3) and add auto-retry fallback to fp16 if quality drifts beyond threshold.
Alex W: thanks — pushing the new scheduler flags to canary now. logs and charts in the shared figma: https://figma.com/file/abcd1234/cont-batcher-runs
Maria P: :thumbsup: please ping when EU 20ms run is live
Alex W: will do. final note: these were short bursts of traffic — need long-run stability test before Dedicated sizing changes.
